newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Laura Ashley to expand home decor.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Laura Ashley to expand home decor.

text.p: Retailer Laura Ashley Holdings Plc said on Tuesday it was developing its higher-margin home furnishings business in the UK and U.S. as part of its three-year recovery programme.

The retailer, famous for its flowery dresses, plans to add more than 100,000 square feet of store space in the U.S. this year mainly via larger format stores, finance director Jim Walsh said in an interview.
The new stores, like one in Atlanta, Georgia which opened in August, have about 15,000 square feet of selling space compared to an average 1,600 square feet in its existing U.S. stores.

In Britain the group is adding 33,000 square feet of space this year, opening 16 new stores and closing six. A stand-alone Laura Ashley out-of-town home furnishing store will open in Warrington in northwest England in November. Another store is opening in Cardiff in south Wales next month, he said.
The group also plans to expand its presence in J. Sainsbury Plc's Homebase stores, where it currently has 65 outlets, Walsh said.
Dino Adriano, deputy chief executive of Sainsbury's supermarkets, has just joined the Laura Ashley board as a non-executive director.
He was until recently chairman of Homebase Group Ltd.

Walsh said the group's restructuring was going to plan. He and fellow merican chief executive Ann Iverson were hired last year to turn round the business, which was strugging after several years of under-investment and over-optimistic expansion.
"At this particular moment in time we are on track. We're where we expected to be with regard to the restructuring."

He said the group was making progress clearing out old stock and reducing costs. Both direct and indirect costs were reduced in total by about six percent in the the first half compared to the first half last year, Walsh said.
The cost reductions more than offset a 1.4 million stg fall in gross margin in the half year in cash terms, he added.
Walsh said the group hopes gross margins and sales will get a boost early next year when the first ranges from Basha Cohen, the new director of design and buying, hit the shops.
The group also plans to re-launch its mail order business next year in both the U.S. and UK. "We've done quite a bit of market research -- there is a definite demand," Walsh said.
Capital sapending this year will be around 18 or 19 million stg, up sharply from last year, he said. There is no debt on the balance sheet and the group has about two million stg cash.
